beats.label: S1 · The Hand's summons
beats.text: Ned accepts the Hand role after Jon Arryn's suspicious death; Jaime shoves young Bran from a tower to hide his incest with Cersei.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the two engines of the whole series: Stark honor pulled south, and the Lannister secret that Ned will die uncovering.

beats.label: S1 · Catelyn arrests Tyrion
beats.text: Catelyn arrests Tyrion for the assassin she blames on the Lannisters; the accusation lights the fuse between the two great houses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Stark-Lannister war of coming seasons starts here, on a wrong guess about who sent the knife.

beats.label: S1 · Joffrey is a Lannister
beats.text: In King's Landing, Ned uncovers that Joffrey and his siblings are Jaime's children, not Robert's — the crown is founded on a lie.
beats.whyLoadBearing: This is the secret every claimant to the throne will fight over for years; Ned's discovery gets him killed.

beats.label: S1 · Robert's death, Ned's trap
beats.text: Robert dies from a boar; Ned tries to install rightful heir Stannis, but Littlefinger betrays him and Joffrey seizes the throne.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Littlefinger as the true operator and cements Joffrey's illegitimate crown, both of which drive years of story.

beats.label: S1 · Ned's beheading
beats.text: Sansa begs for Ned's life; he confesses treason to protect her, but Joffrey has him beheaded anyway on the steps of the Sept.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's founding shock: nobody is safe, and every Stark child's arc from now on runs from this moment.

beats.label: S1 · The North rises
beats.text: Robb marches south, captures Jaime, and is proclaimed King in the North; Arya is smuggled out of King's Landing disguised as a boy.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The war of the Five Kings begins with the Starks splitting from the realm, and Arya's fugitive arc begins.

beats.label: S1 · Dragons return
beats.text: Across the sea, Drogo dies. Daenerys walks into his funeral pyre and emerges unburnt with three newborn dragons on her shoulders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Magic re-enters the world for the first time in centuries; the show's other spine — Daenerys's slow return — is now armed.

cliffhanger.text: Ned is dead. The North has seceded, the Iron Throne sits under an illegitimate boy king, and Robert's brothers Stannis and Renly both claim the crown. Across the Narrow Sea, a Targaryen has hatched living dragons.
questions: Can Robb defeat the Lannisters and get his sisters back?
Will Stannis or Renly enforce the true line of succession before Joffrey does?
What will Daenerys do now that dragons walk the world again?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Ned's bastard son, sworn to the Night's Watch, riding beyond the Wall to search for his missing uncle Benjen.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Widowed Khaleesi with three newborn dragons, followed by Ser Jorah and a small remnant of Drogo's khalasar.

characters.name: Robb Stark
characters.line: Proclaimed King in the North, marching south with an intact army and Jaime Lannister as his prisoner.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: Sent by his father Tywin to King's Landing as acting Hand of the King, to keep Cersei and Joffrey in check.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Hostage of Joffrey in King's Landing after watching her father Ned beheaded on Joffrey's orders.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Smuggled out of King's Landing disguised as a boy by a Night's Watch recruiter, presumed dead by the Lannisters.

beats.label: S2 · Stannis's fire god
beats.text: Stannis Baratheon claims the Iron Throne on Dragonstone, backed by the red priestess Melisandre and her god of fire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Melisandre and Stannis as the third claimant; her shadow magic will kill Renly and shape years of Stannis's story.

beats.label: S2 · Robb marries Talisa
beats.text: Tyrion arrives as acting Hand to rein in Joffrey and Cersei, while Robb falls for the healer Talisa and secretly weds her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Robb breaking his Frey marriage pact is the seed of the Red Wedding, and Tyrion's tenure as Hand starts here.

beats.label: S2 · Theon takes Winterfell
beats.text: Theon returns to the Iron Islands, is scorned by his father Balon, and betrays the Starks by seizing an undefended Winterfell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Theon's betrayal severs the last Stark stronghold from the war and puts Bran and Rickon on the run north.

beats.label: S2 · Arya and Jaqen
beats.text: At Harrenhal, Arya serves Tywin as his cupbearer and befriends Jaqen H'ghar, who repays his debt by killing three people she names.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Arya's introduction to the Faceless Men — the coin Jaqen gives her is the key to her long Braavos arc.

beats.label: S2 · Blackwater
beats.text: Stannis attacks King's Landing; Tyrion holds the city with wildfire until Tywin and the Tyrells arrive to save Joffrey at the last moment.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Stannis is broken, Tyrion is unrewarded and wounded, and the Tyrells now sit next to the throne — the whole KL power map has moved.

beats.label: S2 · Jon among the Wildlings
beats.text: Beyond the Wall, Jon lets himself be captured by the Wildlings on Qhorin's orders; Sam sees the White Walkers marching south with the dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two Northern threads that carry the rest of the show — Jon's cover with the Free Folk and the confirmed White Walker army — both start here.

beats.label: S2 · Bran flees north
beats.text: Theon loses Winterfell to Ramsay's men, who torch it and flay everyone; Bran and Rickon flee north with Osha and Hodor, presumed dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bran's journey toward the Three-Eyed Raven begins; Winterfell now belongs, offscreen, to House Bolton.

cliffhanger.text: Winterfell is a smoking ruin, Bran and Rickon are on the run, and Robb has broken his oath to Walder Frey. Stannis is defeated but not destroyed. Beyond the Wall, an army of the dead has been sighted for the first time.
questions: Will Walder Frey forgive Robb's broken oath?
How will Bran and Rickon survive with no Stark stronghold left?
Can the Night's Watch warn the realm before the dead reach the Wall?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Night's Watch ranger posing as a wildling defector, being led to the King-Beyond-the-Wall Mance Rayder.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Leaving Qarth on a purchased ship with three young dragons after retrieving them from the House of the Undying.

characters.name: Robb Stark
characters.line: Winning the war on the field but has broken his Frey marriage pact by secretly wedding the healer Talisa.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: Wounded and stripped of the Handship after saving King's Landing; his father Tywin has arrived and reclaimed the office.

characters.name: Stannis Baratheon
characters.line: Defeated at the Blackwater with most of his fleet destroyed, but still ridden by Melisandre and her fiery god.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Escaped Harrenhal with Gendry and Hot Pie, carrying a coin from Jaqen that can take her to Braavos.

beats.label: S3 · The Unsullied
beats.text: In Astapor, Daenerys trades a dragon for the Unsullied army — then turns the dragon on the slaver, freeing every slave and leading them out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Daenerys gains the disciplined army she has been missing and commits to the freeing-slaves identity that defines the rest of her arc.

beats.label: S3 · Jaime loses his hand
beats.text: Jaime is captured with Brienne; his sword hand is severed by Locke, forcing him to depend on her and rethink who he is.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Kingslayer without a sword hand is a new character; his slow softening toward Brienne begins the arc that shapes his later choices.

beats.label: S3 · Robb loses his army
beats.text: Robb executes his bannerman Karstark, loses the Karstark forces, and travels to the Twins to remake his broken marriage pact with Walder Frey.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the Red Wedding: Robb needs Frey desperately, and Frey has been publicly humiliated — the trap is being baited.

beats.label: S3 · The Red Wedding
beats.text: At the Twins, Roose Bolton and Walder Frey slaughter Robb, his mother Catelyn, and his pregnant wife Talisa in front of their guests.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The war of the North is over. The remaining Starks are children scattered across the map, and Roose Bolton now holds the North.

beats.label: S3 · Sansa forced to marry Tyrion
beats.text: To seize the Northern claim, Tywin forces Tyrion to wed Sansa; her family is destroyed and she is now a Lannister bride in name.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sansa's marriage is a legal weapon the Lannisters can never quite use — and it locks her into Littlefinger's coming rescue.

beats.label: S3 · Ramsay's plaything
beats.text: In a hidden cellar, Theon is tortured by a smiling stranger who is later revealed as Roose Bolton's cruel bastard son, Ramsay Snow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ramsay is the villain of the next several seasons in the North; Theon's remaking into Reek is happening in real time.

beats.label: S3 · Jon breaks cover
beats.text: Jon refuses to murder a farmer for the Wildlings and flees back to Castle Black; Ygritte fills him with arrows but can't bring herself to kill him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jon returns to the Night's Watch just as the Wildling army is marching on the Wall, which sets up the whole defense next season.

cliffhanger.text: The Starks are broken — Robb and Catelyn dead, Bran heading beyond the Wall for the Three-Eyed Raven, Sansa a Lannister bride, Arya adrift with the Hound. Ramsay has Theon in a cellar, and Daenerys marches on Yunkai with a slave army at her back.
questions: Who avenges the Red Wedding when every remaining Stark is scattered?
Will Stannis answer the Night's Watch's call for aid against the Wildlings?
What does Ramsay want from a broken Theon?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Back at Castle Black wounded, cover blown, warning the Watch that a wildling army of a hundred thousand is coming for the Wall.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Marching with the Unsullied and thousands of freed slaves, hailed as 'Mhysa' — mother — outside the gates of Yunkai.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: Reluctantly married to Sansa, alienated from Tywin, still nominally on the small council but out of his father's favor.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Trapped in King's Landing as Tyrion's wife, all her family either dead or missing after the Red Wedding.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: On the road with the Hound, who arrived at the Twins as the massacre began and is now taking her toward Lysa in the Vale.

characters.name: Jaime Lannister
characters.line: Returned to King's Landing without a sword hand, changed by his captivity, reunited with Cersei but no longer the same man.

beats.label: S4 · The Purple Wedding
beats.text: At his own wedding, Joffrey is poisoned by Olenna Tyrell and Littlefinger; Cersei blames Tyrion in her grief and has him arrested.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the show's central villain, empties the Iron Throne for a pliable child, and puts Tyrion on trial for a crime he didn't commit.

beats.label: S4 · Sansa vanishes
beats.text: Littlefinger smuggles Sansa out of King's Landing to Lysa in the Eyrie, then shoves Lysa through the Moon Door — Sansa lies to save him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sansa is now Littlefinger's pupil, not his hostage; she has consciously chosen to protect a murderer and lie for him.

beats.label: S4 · Meereen and the choice to stay
beats.text: Daenerys captures Meereen, frees its slaves, and decides to stay and rule Slaver's Bay rather than sail on for Westeros.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Daenerys is stuck in Essos for the next several seasons instead of taking her armies west when she plainly could.

beats.label: S4 · Bran reaches the Raven
beats.text: Beyond the Wall, Bran and his party reach the Three-Eyed Raven in his cave of visions after Jojen Reed is killed by wights.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bran's whole future — as seer, as chronicler — begins in this cave, and the White Walkers now know where he is.

beats.label: S4 · The Viper falls
beats.text: Oberyn Martell fights the Mountain in trial by combat for Tyrion but gloats too long over his prone opponent — the Mountain crushes his skull.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Tyrion is condemned to die, Dorne is now blood-feuding with the Lannisters, and Oberyn's paramour Ellaria will not forget.

beats.label: S4 · Tyrion kills Tywin
beats.text: Jaime and Varys break Tyrion out; he strangles his lover Shae in Tywin's bed and shoots his father dead on the privy with a crossbow.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Lannister patriarch is gone, Cersei loses her one restraint, and Tyrion is smuggled to Essos where he'll find Daenerys.

beats.label: S4 · Arya sails east
beats.text: Arya leaves the Hound dying against a boulder and boards a ship for Braavos, using the coin Jaqen H'ghar gave her back at Harrenhal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up Arya's whole Braavos storyline and severs her from Westeros for years.

cliffhanger.text: Tywin is dead on his privy and Tyrion is a fugitive on a ship to Essos. Cersei has lost her father, her son Joffrey, and her control of the Sparrows-adjacent city. Sansa is now Littlefinger's willing conspirator; Daenerys is trying to rule a city that keeps trying to overthrow her; Bran has reached his cave.
questions: Who holds Lannister power now that the patriarch is gone?
Can Daenerys rule a city where the slavers keep coming back?
What can Bran do with the Three-Eyed Raven's gifts?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Commanding respect at Castle Black after driving off the Wildling assault; Stannis has just arrived north with an army.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Queen of Meereen, trying to learn to rule after Astapor and Yunkai have quietly reverted to slavery behind her.

characters.name: Cersei Lannister
characters.line: Queen Mother to the new boy king Tommen, grieving Joffrey, at war with the brother who just murdered their father.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: A fugitive smuggled across the Narrow Sea in a crate by Varys, having killed his father and his lover.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: With Littlefinger in the Vale, now complicit in Lysa's murder and starting to play the game herself.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Alone on a ship to Braavos with a Faceless Man's coin, having left the Hound to die.

beats.label: S5 · Cersei arms the Sparrows
beats.text: Cersei arms the fanatical Sparrows to attack the Tyrells; the trap catches Margaery, then Loras, and eventually herself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cersei creates the religious army that will imprison her and hold King's Landing hostage — the wildfire plot next season starts from here.

beats.label: S5 · Sansa given to Ramsay
beats.text: Littlefinger delivers Sansa to Winterfell as Ramsay Bolton's bride, promising rescue; Ramsay abuses her nightly in front of a broken Theon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts a Stark back inside Winterfell, cracks Theon's Reek persona, and sets up her escape and the retaking of the North.

beats.label: S5 · Tyrion joins Daenerys
beats.text: Tyrion is captured by the exiled Jorah and brought as a gift to Daenerys, who instead accepts him as an advisor in Meereen.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two protagonists of opposite halves of the show finally meet; Tyrion becomes the political brain of Daenerys's court.

beats.label: S5 · The pit and Drogon returns
beats.text: Daenerys weds Hizdahr for peace; at the reopened fighting pit the Sons of the Harpy ambush her, until Drogon returns and flies her off.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Daenerys is now separated from her council in Meereen, alone on a dragon over Dothraki country — that separation drives all of next season's Essos plot.

beats.label: S5 · Stannis burns Shireen
beats.text: To win his march on Winterfell, Stannis lets Melisandre burn his own daughter Shireen alive as a sacrifice — and loses everything anyway.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moral end of Stannis and, effectively, of his claim; sets up his execution by Brienne and Melisandre's flight to Castle Black.

beats.label: S5 · Arya blinded
beats.text: Arya defies the Faceless Men by killing Meryn Trant in personal revenge; Jaqen strips her of her sight as punishment.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Arya's whole training is about becoming 'no one' by giving up personal vengeance — she has just failed, publicly, and now must earn her sight back.

beats.label: S5 · For the Watch
beats.text: Jon lets the Wildlings through the Wall to save them from the dead; his own Night's Watch brothers stab him to death for it in the courtyard.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season ends on Jon dead in the snow — the cliffhanger the whole audience walks back into next season.

cliffhanger.text: Jon lies dead in the snow, killed by his own brothers. Sansa and Theon have just leapt from Winterfell's walls, running from Ramsay. Cersei has been marched naked through King's Landing by the Sparrows she armed. Stannis has been executed by Brienne. Daenerys is lost with Drogon among a Dothraki horde.
questions: Is Jon truly dead, and can Melisandre bring him back?
Will Sansa reach safety before Ramsay recaptures her?
Can Daenerys survive alone among the Dothraki?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Lord Commander of the Night's Watch, stabbed to death in the courtyard of Castle Black by Alliser Thorne and his own steward Olly.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Flown out of Meereen on Drogon and marooned in Dothraki country; her council rules a shaky Meereen without her.

characters.name: Cersei Lannister
characters.line: Freed by the Sparrows only after a naked walk of shame through the city, now back at the Red Keep with Qyburn's Mountain reanimated at her side.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: Governing Meereen in Daenerys's absence alongside Varys, Grey Worm, and Missandei.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Escaped from Winterfell with Theon by jumping into the snow together, running from Ramsay and his hunting dogs.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Punished with blindness by the Faceless Men for stealing a face and killing Meryn Trant for personal revenge.

beats.label: S6 · Jon returns
beats.text: Melisandre resurrects Jon; he executes his murderers, walks away from the Night's Watch, and joins Sansa to retake Winterfell.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's central hero is back and free of his old vow — everything Jon does for the rest of the series follows from this reset.

beats.label: S6 · Ramsay takes the North
beats.text: Ramsay murders his father Roose to seize House Bolton; he lures Jon onto the field by torturing and killing Rickon Stark before his eyes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ramsay becomes the sole Bolton and kills the youngest Stark boy — the confrontation this sets up is the entire back half of the season.

beats.label: S6 · The Night King marks Bran
beats.text: The Night King finds Bran through his visions, kills the Three-Eyed Raven, and marks him — Bran barely escapes north bearing the mantle himself.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Bran is now the Raven, and the Night King has a direct line to him; the war for the living gains an actual timeline.

beats.label: S6 · Daenerys and the Dothraki
beats.text: Daenerys burns the Dothraki khals alive inside their sacred temple and walks out unburnt; the whole horde kneels and follows her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Solves the S5 cliffhanger and gives Daenerys the Dothraki cavalry that fills out her invasion force.

beats.label: S6 · Wildfire in the Sept
beats.text: Cersei destroys the Sept of Baelor with wildfire, killing the High Sparrow, the Tyrells, Lancel, and Kevan; her son Tommen leaps to his death in grief.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cersei has murdered every rival at once, lost her last child, and now has no reason to rule with restraint.

beats.label: S6 · Battle of the Bastards
beats.text: Sansa's secret call brings the Vale's knights to the field at the last moment; Jon defeats Ramsay, who is fed alive to his own starving hounds.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Winterfell is Stark again and Jon is proclaimed King in the North — the setup for his collision with Daenerys and Cersei.

beats.label: S6 · Three claimants, one throne
beats.text: Cersei crowns herself Queen of the Seven Kingdoms; Daenerys sails at last for Westeros with dragons, an armada, and Tyrion as her Hand.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The three claimants — Cersei on the throne, Jon in the North, Daenerys on the sea — are now moving toward each other.

cliffhanger.text: Cersei rules from a hollowed-out King's Landing. Jon rules the North. Daenerys is finally crossing the Narrow Sea with dragons, an armada, and her allies. Bran carries the memory of everything, including a truth about Jon's parents he has not yet shared.
questions: What happens when Cersei, Jon, and Daenerys collide over the same throne?
When will Jon learn what Bran now knows about his true parents?
Can anyone slow the Night King before he reaches the Wall?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Resurrected, released from his Night's Watch vows, proclaimed King in the North after taking Winterfell back from the Boltons.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Sailing at last for Westeros with the Greyjoy fleet, the Dothraki, the Unsullied, three grown dragons, and Tyrion as her Hand.

characters.name: Cersei Lannister
characters.line: Queen of the Seven Kingdoms in her own name, having burned every rival alive; her last living child killed himself in response.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Back at Winterfell alongside Jon but quietly resentful that the Northern lords crowned him and not her, and still in secret contact with Littlefinger.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Back in Westeros with the Faceless Men's face-changing gift, having begun her list of names in earnest.

characters.name: Bran Stark
characters.line: The new Three-Eyed Raven, at the Wall with Meera; his visions have shown him that Jon is the son of Lyanna Stark and Rhaegar Targaryen.

beats.label: S7 · Daenerys lands, Arya strikes
beats.text: Daenerys lands at her ancestral Dragonstone with dragons and armies; in the Riverlands, Arya poisons the surviving lords of House Frey.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Daenerys is finally in Westeros and Arya's list has begun collecting — the two long-delayed storylines both step onto the board this hour.

beats.label: S7 · Highgarden falls
beats.text: Jaime sacks Highgarden and takes its gold; a poisoned Olenna Tyrell confesses on her deathbed that she was the one who killed Joffrey.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Tyrells are extinct, Cersei has funds again, and Jaime finally learns his son was killed by the ally he trusted — quietly loosening the Lannister twin bond.

beats.label: S7 · Jon meets Daenerys
beats.text: Daenerys torches the Lannister army from Drogon; Jon travels to Dragonstone to ask her help against the dead but refuses to bend the knee to her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two protagonists finally meet and immediately deadlock, which is the whole plot engine of the rest of the season.

beats.label: S7 · Viserion dies, the wight is captured
beats.text: Jon leads a raid beyond the Wall to capture a wight; the Night King spears the dragon Viserion out of the sky before they can escape.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The dead now have a weapon that can breach the Wall, and Daenerys has seen the threat with her own eyes.

beats.label: S7 · The summit and Cersei's lie
beats.text: The captured wight is shown at a summit in King's Landing; Cersei feigns joining the alliance while secretly hiring the Golden Company from Essos.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cersei's betrayal is the ticking bomb inside the coalition — Jaime rides north having finally left her over it.

beats.label: S7 · Littlefinger's end
beats.text: At Winterfell, Arya and Sansa turn on Littlefinger together and execute him for his years of manipulation, from Jon Arryn's murder onward.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the show's other great manipulator and unites the Stark sisters, closing a thread that has been open since S1.

beats.label: S7 · The Wall falls
beats.text: Sam and Bran realise Jon is the legitimate Targaryen heir; the Night King, riding the reanimated Viserion, blasts through the Wall at Eastwatch.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two of the show's largest secrets and structures — Jon's parentage and the Wall itself — resolve in the same hour, straight into the final season.

cliffhanger.text: The Wall has fallen and the Night King is marching south on an undead dragon. Jon and Daenerys are lovers who don't yet know they are aunt and nephew, and Cersei has secretly reneged on the alliance she publicly joined.
questions: Can the living stop the Night King now that he has a dragon?
What happens when Jon learns he is Aegon Targaryen and has a stronger claim than Daenerys?
When will Cersei's betrayal be revealed to the North?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Has bent the knee to Daenerys and become her lover, sailing north with her, unaware he is her nephew Aegon Targaryen.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Down to two dragons after losing Viserion to the Night King, allied to Jon in bed and in war.

characters.name: Cersei Lannister
characters.line: Sitting Queen who has publicly joined the alliance against the dead while secretly hiring the Golden Company to hold her throne while others die.

characters.name: Jaime Lannister
characters.line: Riding north alone in the snow, having finally quit Cersei after learning she planned to betray Jon and Daenerys.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Lady of Winterfell in Jon's absence, reconciled with Arya after the two of them executed Littlefinger together.

characters.name: Bran Stark
characters.line: The Three-Eyed Raven at Winterfell, holder of the truth about Jon's parents, which he and Sam have just pieced together.

beats.label: S8 · Jon learns who he is
beats.text: Sam tells Jon he is Aegon Targaryen, Daenerys's nephew and the true heir; Jaime arrives at Winterfell to fight the dead beside them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Jon knowing his parentage is the wedge between him and Daenerys that drives everything after the Long Night.

beats.label: S8 · Arya kills the Night King
beats.text: At the Battle of Winterfell, Arya slips past the White Walkers and stabs the Night King with her Valyrian dagger — the dead crumble in a single stroke.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The White Walker threat that has structured the whole show ends in one hour, freeing the survivors — and Daenerys — to turn on each other.

beats.label: S8 · Rhaegal and Missandei
beats.text: Cersei has Euron ambush Daenerys's fleet, killing Rhaegal from ship-mounted ballistas, and beheads Missandei on the walls in front of Grey Worm and Daenerys.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two blows — a dragon and her closest friend — push Daenerys past the last restraint keeping her from burning the city.

beats.label: S8 · The bells
beats.text: Isolated by grief and betrayal, Daenerys burns King's Landing to the ground on Drogon even after the city rings the bells of surrender.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The heel turn the show has been building for years, and the reason Jon will do what he does next.

beats.label: S8 · The twins die together
beats.text: Jaime returns to Cersei; the two die together as the Red Keep collapses on them, while Arya barely escapes the burning streets.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the Lannister twins in the ruins of the throne they spent the whole series clawing for.

beats.label: S8 · Jon kills Daenerys
beats.text: Jon confronts Daenerys in the throne room and stabs her mid-embrace; Drogon melts the Iron Throne in grief and carries her body away.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The throne everyone has died for is destroyed by the last dragon, and its most likely occupant lies dead in Jon's arms.

beats.label: S8 · A chosen king
beats.text: The lords elect Bran as King of the Six Kingdoms; Sansa wins the North's independence, Arya sails west, and Jon is exiled to the Wall.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Stark children end the series each ruling a piece of what remains, and Jon is sent back where he started.

cliffhanger.text: The wars are over. The Iron Throne is slag, Daenerys is dead, and the realm has just tried something unprecedented — a king chosen rather than born. Bran rules from a rebuilt King's Landing; Sansa rules an independent North; Jon rides beyond the Wall with the Free Folk; Arya sails into uncharted waters.
questions: Will a chosen kingship hold, or will old succession disputes come back?
What lies west of Westeros, where Arya has now sailed off the maps?
Can Jon find peace beyond the Wall after killing the woman he loved?

characters.name: Jon Snow
characters.line: Exiled to the Night's Watch for killing Daenerys, riding north of the Wall with Tormund and the Free Folk.

characters.name: Bran Stark
characters.line: King of the Six Kingdoms — 'Bran the Broken' — chosen by the surviving lords of Westeros in a first-of-its-kind election.

characters.name: Sansa Stark
characters.line: Crowned Queen in the North, having won an independent kingdom back for her house at Bran's coronation.

characters.name: Arya Stark
characters.line: Sailing on a ship of her own commission, headed west of Westeros to explore lands no map has drawn.

characters.name: Tyrion Lannister
characters.line: Hand of King Bran, running a small council of survivors — Brienne, Bronn, Davos, Sam — to rebuild the ruined capital.

characters.name: Daenerys Targaryen
characters.line: Dead, killed by Jon in the throne room after burning King's Landing; her body carried east by Drogon.
